body.condition: Fix the following computational conventions, used for every complexity claim in this paper: (i) for a finite simple bow-free ADMG \(G\) on vertex set \(U\) with \(|U|=n\), singleton target \(s\), and positive rational cost \(c\), the supplied total order on \(U\) induces the order isomorphism \(U\simeq\mathrm{Fin}\,n\), and the instance is encoded as the resulting \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\)-carrier tuple of directed and bidirected adjacency bit-matrices, the index of \(s\), and the numerators and denominators of \(c\) in binary, of encoding length \(L=\operatorname{poly}(n,\operatorname{bitlen}(c))\), while every statement of the form ``\(X\) is computable in polynomial time'' means that the induced map on canonically encoded \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\) instances is computable in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(L\); (ii) all predicates and objective values appearing in this paper, namely \(\mathcal C(G,s)\), \(r(G,s)\), \(\operatorname{LP}(G,s,c)\), \(\operatorname{OPT}(G,s,c)\), and feasibility of an intervention set, are invariant under vertex relabeling, so a polynomial-time algorithm on the canonical \(\mathrm{Fin}\,n\) carrier transfers to any finite vertex type \(U\) via the supplied order with polynomial overhead; (iii) an algorithm performing \(\operatorname{poly}(n,L)\) elementary operations on encoded instances, consisting of graph adjacency queries, reachability and ancestor searches, comparisons, and field operations on rationals of bit length \(\operatorname{poly}(L)\), runs in time \(\operatorname{poly}(n,L)\); and (iv) the class of polynomial-time maps on canonically encoded instances is closed under composition, in particular under composition of the private-guard expansion, parent-spouse rounding, and reverse guard-replacement map.
